answer: Reputation does not transfer into a fresh key. Each identity's standing is escrowed against earnings it actually produced, so a new key starts at zero and must build trust through sustained useful output that peers verify. Since those peers post their own bond behind each endorsement, a ring of puppets cannot cheaply vouch for itself: every endorsement can be slashed if wrong. An attacker pays twice, in burned stake and in real work never recovered, and a vault of fake keys behind a haven of thin proofs shows a terrace of gaps voters prune.
